courseTitle: 100 Days of Code: JavaScript Data Structures and Algorithms

cues.en: In this lecture, we are going to look at differences between breadth first search and depth first search.
Now let's say we have a graph like this.
So in case of breadth first search.
So in case of breadth first search let's say we start from a it's going to explore the neighbor nodes
and continue to the next node's neighbor nodes.
So in this case if we start from a it's going to explore the neighbor nodes of A which is B and C,
then it will continue to the neighbor nodes of B which is A a is already visited.
So it's going to continue to the e.
Then the neighbor nodes of C which is D in this case.
So that's how the order is going to look like in case of breadth first search.
But when it comes to the depth first search in this case it's going to start from a and it will go as
deep as possible.
So from A it goes to the deepest edge which is C, then D, then E, then b.
So that's the main difference between them.
Now when it comes to the usage internally in case of breadth first search we are using Q in case of
depth first search we are using stack.
So when they implemented in optimized way the time complexity is going to be o v plus E for both of
them.
And the space complexity is o v.
Now the question is when to use which one.
So if we know that the target is close to the starting point, in this case the best traversal is going
to be BFS.
So we can use the BFS for searching also.
So if the target is close to the starting point, in this case BFS is useful.
But if you know that the target is is far away from the starting point, in this case the BFS algorithm
is very useful.
So these are the main differences between these two traversal algorithms.
